deploy-bot: ALERT: canary error_rate(5m)=4.9% (baseline 0.6%), deploy=release/v3.9.2-canary
Alex T.: saw the spike. affected route: /v1/embeddings (slice 8%).
Priya R.: any schema or tokenizer changes in this release?
Jordan C.: no schema changes. we changed batching heuristic and kernel selection for small sequences. might be an edge perf bug.
Alex T.: preference: partial revert of the canary pool image to avoid fleet pin. who can execute?
Priya R.: I can do it. plan: 1) lock auto-rollout 2) demote canary image to release/v3.9.1 3) monitor 20m 4) decide on full pin if noisy.
Release-Bot: auto-rollout requirement: human lock required for canary demote.
Jordan C.: run commands: ``/deploy lock auto-rollout --by Priya R.`` then ``/deploy demote-image --pool canary --to release/v3.9.1 --reason "canary error spike"``
Priya R.: locking now and demoting. tagging @Alex T. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
deploy-bot: DEMOTE STARTED: job_id=dem-20260501-07, initiated_by=Priya R., target=canary
Ops-Bot: NOTE: dedicated pools unaffected; release notes flag: batching-heuristic toggled in 3.9.2.
deploy-bot: DEMOTE COMPLETE: job_id=dem-20260501-07, status=success, new_active_image=release/v3.9.1
Alex T.: starting 20m observation window. suppressing noisy alerts for 25m.
Jordan C.: follow-ups: open rollback postmortem ticket, add test that simulates small sequence batching, consider canary traffic reduction next attempt.
Priya R.: I'll post an internal status and notify release manager. reopening rollout only after triage + CI fix.
Release-Bot: INCIDENT RECORDED: incident/2026-05-01-canary-batch-regression, owners=[Priya R., Jordan C., Alex T.], severity=high
Priya R.: thanks team. moving notes to #postmortems in 30m. :white_check_mark:
